# Pre-integrated agents

> Run agents supported by Harbor.

Harbor includes integrations for many agents so that you don't have to install any dependencies.

> [tab] CLI
>
> ```bash theme={"system"}
> export OPENAI_API_KEY="..."
> harbor run \

>

>     }
>   ],
>   "tasks": [

>     }
>   ]

> ```

> import asyncio
>
> from harbor.job import Job
> from harbor.models.job.config import JobConfig
> from harbor.models.trial.config import AgentConfig, TaskConfig

> async def main():

## Agent options

`--effort`, `--ak`, and `--ae` are commonly used agent flags. Run
`harbor run --help` to see the full set.

| Flag | Purpose |
| - | - |
| `--ak`, `--agent-kwarg` | Pass a setting to the agent implementation. Values such as numbers, booleans, lists, and objects are parsed into their corresponding types. |
| `--ae`, `--agent-env` | Set an environment variable during agent setup and execution. Values remain strings. |
| `--effort` | Set reasoning effort for supported agents. Accepted levels depend on the agent and model. |

> [accordion] Antigravity CLI gateway reasoning effort
>
> For `antigravity-cli` gateway runs, `reasoning_effort` accepts `low`, `medium`,
> `high`, `xhigh`, and `max`. Harbor forwards the selected value as `--effort`
> without translating it. The installed Antigravity version and model catalog must
> support that level; accepting the option in Harbor does not add model support.
> Omit the option to use the model's default effort. `none` is not accepted.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Each agent supports its own kwargs and environment variables. Check the
> agent's integration before setting them.

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor run \
  -t hello-world/hello-world \
  -a claude-code -m anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 \
  --ak max_turns=20 \
  --ae MCP_TIMEOUT=20000
```

Here, `max_turns=20` configures the Claude Code integration, while
`MCP_TIMEOUT` is available to the agent process. Both flags can be **repeated**.

Load native config file for corresponding agent. Check out [Claude Code settings.json](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings) and

file:

```bash theme={"system"}

harbor run ... -a codex --ak "config=path/to/config.toml"
```

Inline JSON is also supported. Harbor converts inline JSON to the agent's native config file format and passes it to the agent:

```bash theme={"system"}
# Inline config
harbor run ... -a codex --ak 'config={"model_context_window": 200000}'
```

### Pre-installed agents

If the task image already contains the agent, for example because the
sandbox has no internet access, skip the install with `skip_install`:

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor run ... -a opencode --ak skip_install=true
```

Harbor then trusts the image to provide the agent and everything it needs to
run, including system packages. Steps that depend on the run, such as
uploading Harbor's runner scripts or writing the agent's config, still run.
The recorded agent version is the one the image provides. This option works
for every installed agent. The image must use the paths and runtime expected
by that integration; use `--install-only` to prepare it.

`claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode`, and `opencode-v2` reuse the version installed
in the image if it matches the requested `version`, or if no version is
specified. Otherwise, they install the requested version (latest if unspecified).

# Verifier

> Task verification.

The `tests/test.sh` script is the entrypoint for the verifier. Harbor uploads `tests/` to `/tests/` after the agent runs, unless a [dedicated verifier image or build definition](#separate-verifier-environment) provides the tests. `tests/test.sh` is executed in the task's working directory and is responsible for verifying the task's completion. It must produce a numerical reward at `/logs/verifier/reward.txt` or `/logs/verifier/reward.json`.

## Required script

| OS | File |
| - | - |
| Linux | `tests/test.sh` |
| Windows | `tests/test.bat` |

Install test dependencies in `tests/Dockerfile` (or the agent image for shared verification). The script should:

1. Verify that the agent satisfied the [instruction](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/instruction.md)
2. Write a **reward** under `/logs/verifier/`

We recommend using **absolute paths** inside the script to avoid `cwd` surprises.

## Reward files

| File | Format |
| - | - |
| `/logs/verifier/reward.json` | JSON key-value object of labeled numeric metrics |
| `/logs/verifier/reward.txt` | Single number, usually `1` or `0` |

If both are present, Harbor prefers `reward.json`.

### Example

```bash title="tests/test.sh" theme={"system"}
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

if pytest /tests/test_outputs.py; then
  echo 1 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
else
  echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
fi
```

For multi-metric or LLM-based grading, consider using [RewardKit](https://docs.harborframework.com/rewardkit/quick-start.md) or writing a structured `reward.json` file.

## Separate verifier environment

Tasks created with `harbor task init` or `harbor init --task` configure a separate sandbox for verification. Omitting both `verifier.environment_mode` and `[verifier.environment]` uses shared verification.

To opt into shared verification, set `environment_mode = "shared"` under `[verifier]` in `task.toml`, omit `[verifier.environment]`, and install verifier dependencies in the agent image.

Harbor prefers `[verifier.environment].docker_image`, then a build definition in `tests/` (`Dockerfile` or `docker-compose.yaml`), over the agent environment. These dedicated verifier images must include `/tests/test.sh` or `/tests/test.bat`; Harbor does not upload tests into them at runtime.

Without a dedicated verifier image or build definition, Harbor starts a fresh copy of the agent environment and uploads `tests/` to `/tests/`. The agent's filesystem changes are not inherited. For multi-step tasks, step verifier definitions take precedence over task-level definitions.

Declare [artifacts](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/artifacts.md) in the top-level `artifacts` list in `task.toml`, before any section headers. Harbor collects them before verification and copies them into the separate verifier sandbox at their original source paths.

See [Separate verifier](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/separate-verifier.md) for more details.

### Example

```toml title="task.toml" theme={"system"}
[verifier]
environment_mode = "separate"

[verifier.environment]
cpus = 2
```

```dockerfile title="tests/Dockerfile" theme={"system"}
FROM python:3.12-slim

COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.9.7 /uv /usr/local/bin/uv

RUN uv pip install --system pytest==8.4.1 pytest-json-ctrf==0.3.5

WORKDIR /app

COPY . /tests/
```

## Regrading

Harbor can rerun verifiers for existing trials if the task uses a separate verifier environment. This is useful when iterating on a verifier.

See [Regrade](https://docs.harborframework.com/jobs/regrade.md) for details.

## Passing environment variables to the verifier

Environment variables can be passed to the verifier using the `[verifier.env]` section in `task.toml`.

```toml title="task.toml" theme={"system"}
[verifier.env]
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}"
MODEL_NAME = "claude-haiku-4-5"
```

The `${VAR}` syntax is used to read from the host environment. Harbor will ask the user to confirm before passing the environment variables to the verifier.

## LLM- or agent-as-a-judge

Task authors can implement `test.sh` to use whatever verification approach they like, including LLM- or agent-as-a-judge.

To avoid boilerplate, consider using [RewardKit](https://docs.harborframework.com/rewardkit/quick-start.md) to define your judge or programmatic criteria.

## `rewardkit`

The Harbor team maintains a package called [`harbor-rewardkit`](https://docs.harborframework.com/rewardkit/quick-start). It is the easiest way to define and run common verifiers, including programmatic criteria and LLM- or agent-as-a-judge.

# Solution

> Task solutions.

The **`solution/`** folder is **optional**. It holds a reference script used by the oracle agent to sanity-check that a task is solvable. Solutions often help when debugging tasks or sandbox integrations.

## Required script

| OS | File |
| - | - |
| Linux | `solution/solve.sh` |
| Windows | `solution/solve.bat` |

Harbor chooses the extension from `[environment].os` in [task.toml](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/configuration.md).

Additional files (scripts, data) are allowed. At runtime Harbor copies the folder to `/solution` and runs the solve script from the task working directory.

## When to include a solution

* **Recommended** while authoring tasks — run `harbor run` with the Oracle agent to verify the task is solvable.
* **Optional** for published benchmarks — omit if you do not want a public reference implementation.

Without `solution/`, the Oracle agent cannot run.

## Configuration

```toml title="task.toml" theme={"system"}
[solution]
env = { API_KEY = "sk-test-123" }
```

Variables are applied when the Oracle executes `solve.sh`.

## Multiple solutions

Use `--ae` to pass an environment variable, then choose an implementation in `solution/solve.sh`. **You choose the variable name and write the selection logic in `solve.sh`, so you can support as many solutions as you need.** It can run `solve2.sh`, `solution2/solve.sh`, a Python script, or any other implementation. Harbor copies the entire `solution/` directory, so implementations can share helpers or use separate supporting files.

The [hello-world-multiple-solutions example](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/tree/main/examples/tasks/hello-world-multiple-solutions) uses `SOLUTION` to select a second correct solution. From the repository root:

```bash theme={"system"}
uv run harbor run -p examples/tasks/hello-world-multiple-solutions -a oracle \
  --ae SOLUTION=2
```

Omit `--ae` to run the original solution. Both should receive reward `1`. `SOLUTION` is just this example's choice, not a special Harbor variable. Avoid setting the same variable in `[solution.env]`, which takes precedence over `--ae`.

# ATIF

> Record and exchange agent trajectories in a standard JSON format.

The **Agent Trajectory Interchange Format (ATIF)** records an agent's complete
interaction history as JSON: messages, reasoning, tool calls, observations, and
metrics.

## Why

Agents produce [different native logs](https://docs.harborframework.com/jobs/loading-trajectories.md#native-trajectories).
Without a shared format, every viewer, dataset, and training pipeline needs an
agent-specific parser. ATIF provides one stable representation across agents,
making trajectories easier to inspect, compare, validate, load, and reuse.

See the [ATIF RFC](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/main/rfcs/0001-trajectory-format.md)
for the complete specification.

## `trajectory.json` in Harbor

> [!NOTE]
>
> In Harbor, an ATIF trajectory is usually named **`trajectory.json`**.

Agents with `capabilities.atif = true` write it to the agent log directory. In a
downloaded trial result, the path is `agent/trajectory.json`.

Harbor uses this file to:

* **Render trajectories:** The [results viewer](https://docs.harborframework.com/results/view-job-results.md#start-the-viewer)
  reads `agent/trajectory.json` and displays its steps in the **Trajectory** tab.
* **Load trajectories:** Supported agents can use an
  [ATIF trajectory](https://docs.harborframework.com/jobs/loading-trajectories.md#atif-trajectories) to seed a new
  session.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Producing ATIF and loading ATIF are separate capabilities. An agent may write
> `trajectory.json` without supporting [loading trajectories](https://docs.harborframework.com/jobs/loading-trajectories.md).

Custom agents should declare `AgentCapabilities(atif=True)` only when they write
a valid `self.logs_dir / "trajectory.json"`.

## Structure

Harbor's current format is `ATIF-v1.8`. A trajectory contains:

| Field | Purpose |
| - | - |
| `agent` | Agent name, version, model, and optional tool definitions. |
| `steps` | Ordered system, user, and agent interactions. |
| `session_id` | Optional identifier shared by trajectories from one run. |
| `trajectory_id` | Optional document identifier; required for embedded subagents. |
| `final_metrics` | Optional aggregate token, cost, and step metrics. |
| `subagent_trajectories` | Optional embedded ATIF trajectories. |
| `extra` | Custom root-level metadata. |

Step IDs start at `1` and remain sequential. Agent steps can include
`tool_calls`, matching `observation` results, and per-step `metrics`.

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "schema_version": "ATIF-v1.8",
  "session_id": "session-123",
  "agent": {
    "name": "my-agent",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "model_name": "openai/gpt-5.6-sol"
  },
  "steps": [
    {
      "step_id": 1,
      "source": "user",
      "message": "Create hello.txt."
    },
    {
      "step_id": 2,
      "source": "agent",
      "message": "I'll create it.",
      "tool_calls": [
        {
          "tool_call_id": "call-1",
          "function_name": "write_file",
          "arguments": {"path": "hello.txt", "content": "Hello"}
        }
      ],
      "observation": {
        "results": [
          {"source_call_id": "call-1", "content": "File created"}
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> [accordion] Build with Harbor models
>
> Harbor provides Pydantic models in `harbor.models.trajectories`:
>
> ```python theme={"system"}
> import json
> from pathlib import Path
>
> from harbor.models.trajectories import Agent, Step, Trajectory
>
> trajectory = Trajectory(
>     agent=Agent(name="my-agent", version="1.0.0"),
>     steps=[
>         Step(step_id=1, source="user", message="Create hello.txt."),
>         Step(step_id=2, source="agent", message="Done."),
>     ],
> )
>
> Path("trajectory.json").write_text(
>     json.dumps(trajectory.to_json_dict(), indent=2) + "\n"
> )
> ```

## Validate a trajectory

```bash theme={"system"}
uv run python -m harbor.utils.trajectory_validator path/to/trajectory.json
```

Validation checks the schema, sequential step IDs, tool-call references,
timestamps, and referenced local images. Use `--no-validate-images` to skip the
image-file check.

> [accordion] Validate in Python
>
> ```python theme={"system"}
> from harbor.utils.trajectory_validator import TrajectoryValidator
>
> validator = TrajectoryValidator()
>
> if not validator.validate("trajectory.json"):
>     for error in validator.get_errors():
>         print(error)
> ```

## Versions and extensions

Harbor accepts `ATIF-v1.0` through `ATIF-v1.8`. Version 1.8 adds audio content
parts with referenced audio files and optional durations. Version 1.7 adds embedded
subagent trajectories, per-document trajectory IDs, `llm_call_count`, and
additional extension fields. See the
[RFC changelog](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/main/rfcs/0001-trajectory-format.md#version-history)
for earlier versions.

> [!TIP]
>
> Use the schema's `extra` fields for custom metadata. Harbor's Pydantic models
> reject undeclared fields.

## Resources

[ATIF RFC](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/main/rfcs/0001-trajectory-format.md), [Harbor trajectory models](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/tree/main/src/harbor/models/trajectories), [Valid trajectory examples](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/tree/main/tests/golden), [Trajectory validator](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/main/src/harbor/utils/trajectory_validator.py)

# Configuration

> Task configuration, metadata, and schema reference.

The **`task.toml`** file specifies the task configuration and metadata.

```toml theme={"system"}
schema_version = "1.4"

[task]
name = "apple/create-unix-os"
authors = [{ name = "Steve Jobs", email = "steve@apple.com" }]

[metadata]
difficulty_explanation = "Trivial task for demonstration"
category = "programming"

[verifier]
timeout_sec = 120.0
env = { API_KEY = "sk-test-123" }
user = "root"  # optional: run the verifier as this OS user

[agent]
timeout_sec = 120.0
user = "agent"  # optional: run the agent as this OS user

[solution]
env = { API_KEY = "sk-test-123" }

[environment]
network_mode = "allowlist"  # baseline; defaults to "public" when omitted
allowed_hosts = ["pypi.org"]
docker_image = "apple/unix-os:latest"
cpus = 1
memory_mb = 2048
storage_mb = 10240
```

## `[environment]` vs. `environment/`

By default, Harbor defers as much configuration as possible into the `environment/` spec rather than the `task.toml`. A lot of engineering effort has gone into designing `environment/` specs (like `Dockerfile`) and they provide conventions for common use cases.

Only when absolutely necessary does Harbor require configuration in the `task.toml`.

A few fields in `task.toml` are due to lack of convention or common pitfalls:

| Field | Explanation |
| - | - |
| `environment.docker_image` | Specifies the Docker image to use for the environment. (If this is set, `environment/` can be omitted entirely) |
| `environment.network_mode` | Sets the network isolation mode (e.g., `public`, `allowlist`). |
| `environment.allowed_hosts` | Lists domains/IPs allowed for outbound network access when `network_mode` is `allowlist`. |
| `environment.env` | Defines environment variables to inject into the environment. |
| `environment.healthcheck` | Configuration for checking if the environment is healthy or ready. |
| `environment.workdir` | Sets the working directory for commands run in the environment. This was added by popular demand to retroactively set a `workdir` without having to rebuild the image. |

## Field reference

### General

**schema\_version** `string` (default: "1.4")

Version of the task configuration format.

**multi\_step\_reward\_strategy** `"mean" | "final" | null` (default: null)

How to derive the trial-level reward from per-step verifier results. Only applies when `[[steps]]` is set; leave unset for single-step tasks (defaults to "mean" on multi-step). See [Multi-step](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/multi-step.md).

### `[task]`

**task** `PackageInfo | null` (default: null)

Optional \[task] section for registry package metadata. When present, task.name is required.

**task.name** `string`

Package name in org/name format (e.g., "harbor/hello-world"). Required when \[task] is declared.

**task.authors** `list[Author]` (default: \[])

List of task authors. Each entry has a required name and optional email (for example, `[{ name = "Jane", email = "jane@example.com" }]`).

**task.description** `string` (default: "")

Human-readable description of the task.

**task.keywords** `list[string]` (default: \[])

Keywords for search and categorization.

### `[metadata]`

**metadata** `object`

Arbitrary metadata provided by the task author.

### `[verifier]`

**verifier.timeout\_sec** `number` (default: 600)

Timeout in seconds for the verifier.

**verifier.network\_mode** `"no-network" | "public" | "allowlist" | null` (default: null (no override))

Optional override during verify(). Applied only when set and different from the verifier baseline. See [Network policies](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/network-policies.md).

**verifier.allowed\_hosts** `list[string] | null` (default: null)

Allowlist hostnames when verifier.network\_mode is allowlist.

**verifier.env** `object` (default: \{})

Environment variables to set when running the verifier.

**verifier.user** `string | int | null` (default: null)

Username or UID to run the verifier as. When set, the environment's default user is configured accordingly before verification. If not set, the environment's container default (typically root) is used.

**verifier.environment\_mode** `"shared" | "separate" | null` (default: null)

Where the verifier runs. "shared" (default when both this field and \[verifier.environment] are omitted) reuses the agent's container; "separate" launches a dedicated verifier container with its own image. Omitting this field while declaring \[verifier.environment] implies "separate". Declaring "shared" alongside \[verifier.environment] is a validation error.

**verifier.environment** `EnvironmentConfig | null` (default: null)

Optional verifier configuration, using the same schema as `[environment]`. Verifier images and `tests/` build definitions take precedence over the agent environment. Dedicated verifier images must bundle tests; falling back to the agent environment uploads them to `/tests/`. See [Image selection](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/separate-verifier.md#image-selection).

**verifier.environment.network\_mode** `"no-network" | "public" | "allowlist"` (default: "public")

Separate verifier env baseline when \[verifier.environment] is set. Same modes as environment.network\_mode.

**verifier.environment.allowed\_hosts** `list[string] | null` (default: null)

Allowlist hostnames when verifier.environment.network\_mode is allowlist.

### `[agent]`

**agent.timeout\_sec** `number | null` (default: null)

Timeout in seconds for the agent. If not set, no timeout is enforced.

**agent.network\_mode** `"no-network" | "public" | "allowlist" | null` (default: null (no override))

Optional override during agent.run(). Applied only when set and different from \[environment]. See [Network policies](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/network-policies.md).

**agent.allowed\_hosts** `list[string] | null` (default: null)

Allowlist hostnames when agent.network\_mode is allowlist.

**agent.user** `string | int | null` (default: null)

Username or UID to run the agent as. When set, the environment's default user is configured accordingly before agent setup and execution. If not set, the environment's container default (typically root) is used.

### `[solution]`

**solution.env** `object` (default: \{})

Environment variables to set when running the solution.

### `[environment]`

**environment.build\_timeout\_sec** `number` (default: 600)

Timeout in seconds for environment build.

**environment.network\_mode** `"no-network" | "public" | "allowlist"` (default: "public")

Agent env baseline. Also the shared verifier baseline when no separate verifier env overrides it. See [Network policies](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/network-policies.md).

**environment.allowed\_hosts** `list[string] | null` (default: null)

Allowlist hostnames when environment.network\_mode is allowlist.

**environment.docker\_image** `string | null` (default: null)

A pre-built Docker image to use for the environment. When set, environment/Dockerfile is optional for supported environment types.

**environment.os** `"linux" | "windows"` (default: "linux")

Target operating system for the task container. "linux" (default) or "windows". When "windows", Harbor uses Windows-style paths, cmd.exe execution, tar-over-exec file transfer, and filters script discovery to .bat only. The Docker daemon mode and image OS are validated against this value at start; mismatches fail fast.

**environment.cpus** `number | null` (default: null)

Number of CPUs requested by the task. When omitted, Harbor leaves CPU sizing to the selected provider. Fractional values require [provider support](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/resources.md#provider-support).

**environment.memory\_mb** `integer | null` (default: null)

Amount of RAM requested by the task in megabytes. When omitted, Harbor leaves memory sizing to the selected provider.

**environment.storage\_mb** `integer | null` (default: null)

Amount of storage requested by the task in megabytes. When omitted, Harbor leaves storage sizing to the selected provider.

**environment.gpus** `integer | null` (default: null)

Number of GPUs requested by the task. When omitted, Harbor does not request GPUs.

**environment.gpu\_types** `list[string] | null` (default: null)

List of acceptable GPU types (e.g., \['H100', 'A100', 'T4']). None means any GPU type is acceptable.

**environment.tpu** `TpuSpec | null` (default: null)

TPU slice specification (type + topology). When set, the environment requests a TPU node matching this spec; per-pod chip count is derived from the topology. Singular because a task allocates exactly one TPU slice per pod. Only supported on TPU-capable environments (currently GKE).

**environment.tpu.type** `string`

TPU accelerator type. Accepts either a user-friendly alias (e.g., 'v6e', 'trillium', 'v4') or a canonical GKE label (e.g., 'tpu-v6e-slice', 'tpu7x').

**environment.tpu.topology** `string`

TPU topology as 'NxM' or 'NxMxK' (e.g., '2x4', '2x2x1'). Required — GKE's implicit default topology is not part of a stable contract, so omitting it would make Harbor runs non-reproducible across GKE versions. Per-pod TPU chip count is computed as the product of dimensions (e.g. '2x2x1' → 4 chips, '2x4' → 8 chips). Each dimension must be a positive integer (no leading zeros).

**environment.allow\_internet** `boolean | null` (default: null)

Deprecated compatibility field. Prefer \[environment].network\_mode. When set and \[environment].network\_mode is omitted, false maps to no-network and true maps to public.

**environment.env** `object` (default: \{})

Environment variables required for the task, resolved from the host at runtime. Supports `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` template syntax.

**environment.mcp\_servers.name** `string`

Unique name for each MCP server entry (declare servers as `[[environment.mcp_servers]]` in TOML). Compatible agents register them automatically. See [MCPs](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/environment.md#mcps).

**environment.mcp\_servers.transport** `"stdio" | "sse" | "streamable-http"` (default: "sse")

How the agent connects to the server. "sse" and "streamable-http" require url; "stdio" requires command. Legacy value "http" is normalized to "streamable-http".

**environment.mcp\_servers.url** `string | null` (default: null)

Endpoint URL when transport is "sse" or "streamable-http" (e.g. [http://mcp-server:8000/mcp](http://mcp-server:8000/mcp) for a Compose sidecar). Required for those transports.

**environment.mcp\_servers.headers** `object[string, string]` (default: \{})

HTTP request headers for "sse" and "streamable-http" servers. Values support embedded `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` references resolved when the agent starts. Credential headers must use `${VAR}` references. Headers are invalid for "stdio" servers. See [MCPs](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/environment.md#mcps).

**environment.mcp\_servers.command** `string | null` (default: null)

Executable to spawn when transport is "stdio". Required for stdio.

**environment.mcp\_servers.args** `list[string]` (default: \[])

Arguments passed to command when transport is "stdio".

**environment.skills\_dir** `string | null` (default: null)

Path to a [skills directory](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/skills.md) in the environment. Contents are registered with compatible agents.

**environment.healthcheck** `HealthcheckConfig | null` (default: null)

Optional healthcheck block run after environment start (omit the whole \[environment.healthcheck] section to disable). When set, command is required; other fields use the defaults below.

**environment.healthcheck.command** `string`

Shell command to run as a healthcheck after environment start. Exit 0 means healthy. Required when \[environment.healthcheck] is present.

**environment.healthcheck.interval\_sec** `number` (default: 5)

Time in seconds between healthcheck attempts.

**environment.healthcheck.timeout\_sec** `number` (default: 30)

Maximum time in seconds for a single healthcheck command.

**environment.healthcheck.start\_period\_sec** `number` (default: 0)

Grace period in seconds after environment start during which failures don't count.

**environment.healthcheck.start\_interval\_sec** `number` (default: 5)

Interval in seconds between checks during the start period.

**environment.healthcheck.retries** `integer` (default: 3)

Number of consecutive failures before the healthcheck is considered failed.

**environment.workdir** `string | null` (default: null)

Default working directory for command execution in the environment. Overrides the container WORKDIR when set.

### Artifacts

**artifacts** `list[string | ArtifactConfig]` (default: \[])

Root-level paths to snapshot from the environment into the trial artifacts directory after the agent runs, before verification. For multi-step tasks, these paths are included in every step's collection pass, alongside `[[steps]].artifacts` — see [Multi-step](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/multi-step.md). Each entry is a container path string or a table with source / destination / exclude. See [Artifacts](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/artifacts.md) for examples.

**artifacts.source** `string`

Container path to download (file or directory). Required for table entries; a bare string in the artifacts list is shorthand for source only.

**artifacts.destination** `string | null` (default: null)

Relative path under the trial artifacts directory. When omitted, Harbor derives the host path from source.

**artifacts.exclude** `list[string]` (default: \[])

Glob patterns to exclude when source is a directory (passed as tar --exclude flags).

### Provenance

**source** `string | null` (default: null)

Optional source string for task provenance.

## Multi-step configuration

The field reference above covers single-step and shared task-root settings. Multi-step tasks add `[[steps]]` entries with per-step `agent`, `verifier`, `healthcheck`, `min_reward`, and `artifacts` overrides. Step fields, `workdir/setup.sh`, and trial-level reward rollup are documented on [multi-step tasks](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/multi-step.md).

## TOML templates

During task creation, you can pass a `--metadata-template` flag with a path to a TOML file to pre-populate `task.toml` with metadata fields and config defaults:

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor task init [org]/[name] --metadata-template task-template.toml
```

Sections in the template override Harbor's built-in defaults. Newly scaffolded tasks set `verifier.environment_mode = "separate"` unless the template overrides it; other omitted settings use the defaults listed above.

> ```

> [tab] Hub dataset
>
> ```bash theme={"system"}

> ```

> [tab] Hub task
>
> ```bash theme={"system"}
> harbor run -t "<org/task>@<ref>" -a "<agent>" -m "<model>"
> ```

> [tab] Custom registry
>

> ```

> ```

>
> ```bash theme={"system"}
> harbor run -p "<path>" -a "<agent>" -m "<model>" \
>   -o "<jobs-dir>" --job-name "<job-name>"
> ```

> [tab] Concurrency and retries
>
> ```bash theme={"system"}
> harbor run -p "<path>" -a "<agent>" -m "<model>" \
>   -n "<concurrent>" -k "<attempts>" -r "<retries>"
> ```

> [tab] Task filters
>

> harbor run -p "<path>" -a "<agent>" -m "<model>" \
>   -l "<max-tasks>" -i "<some-*-glob-pattern>" -x "<some-name>"
> ```

>

> ```
>
> See [Simulate a user](https://docs.harborframework.com/jobs/simulate-a-user.md).

Run `harbor run --help` to see all available flags.

## Agents

Harbor has pre-integrated agents and support for custom agents.

Run `harbor run --help` to see the available agents.

Set reasoning effort with `--effort`, other agent options with `--ak`, and the model with `--model` (`-m`).

See [Model name parsing](https://docs.harborframework.com/agents/agent-auth-resolution.md#model-name-parsing) to look up how LiteLLM parses a model name.

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor run -a "<agent>" -m "<model>" --effort high
```

See [Pre-integrated agents](https://docs.harborframework.com/agents/pre-integrated-agents.md) or [Custom agents](https://docs.harborframework.com/agents/custom-agents.md) to learn more.

## Config files

Under the hood, configuring a job with CLI flags builds a `JobConfig` object and passes it to the runner.

You can see the config when you run `harbor run` with the `--print-config` flag, or by inspecting the `<job/path>/config.json` file after you run `harbor run`. You can also use `harbor job init` to create and save a config instead of running the job.

For frequent setups, we recommend creating and version controlling your configs.

> [!NOTE]
>
> You can pair a config with CLI flags to override values in the original config.

```json theme={"system"}

  "n_concurrent_trials": 100,
  "retry": {
    "max_retries": 3
  },
  "agents": [
    {
      "name": "<agent>",
      "model_name": "<model>"
    }
  ],
  "datasets": [
    {
      "path": "<path>"
    }
  ]
}
```

See [Configs](https://docs.harborframework.com/jobs/configs.md) for the complete job config schema.

## Run on Harbor Hub

You can run your jobs on Harbor Hub by including the `--launch` flag.

Harbor Hub

* Orchestrates your trials in the cloud
* Enforces per-provider concurrency limits
* Pauses on cascading failures (e.g. usage limits)
* Backs off on rate limits
* Can be accessed using the UI or CLI to debug, trigger retries, share results, or monitor progress

First, sign in.

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor auth login
```

Then, run your job with the `--launch` flag.

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor run -d "<org/name>" -a "<agent>" -m "<model>" \
  -n "<concurrent>" --one-off-secret "<name>=<value>" --launch
```

See [Hosted jobs](https://docs.harborframework.com/harbor-hub/hosted-jobs.md) for more information about evaluating custom agents and Git-based tasks and datasets.

All were HTTP 200, and the content is from the docs site, not a stored copy.

### (1) Task format

**Folder structure** (`/tasks/overview`):
```
my-task/
├── instruction.md
├── task.toml
├── environment/      # Dockerfile or other spec (may be omitted if [environment].docker_image is set)
├── solution/         # solve.sh (Linux) or solve.bat (Windows); optional
└── tests/            # test.sh (Linux) or test.bat (Windows)
```
Multi-step tasks use `steps/step-N/{instruction.md,tests/,solution/,workdir/}` plus `[[steps]]` in `task.toml`. Local-only files can be excluded with `.harborignore` inside `tests/` or `solution/` (Git ignore syntax). Image builds also need `.dockerignore`.

**task.toml fields** (`/tasks/configuration`, `schema_version` example "1.4"):
- Top level: `schema_version` (default "1.4"), `multi_step_reward_strategy` (`"mean" | "final" | null`), `artifacts` (list of strings or tables with `source`, `destination`, `exclude`), `source`.
- `[task]`: `name` (required if `[task]` present, `org/name` form), `authors` (list of `{name, email?}`), `description`, `keywords`.
- `[metadata]`: arbitrary, e.g. `difficulty_explanation`, `category`.
- `[verifier]`: `timeout_sec` (default 600), `network_mode` (`"no-network" | "public" | "allowlist" | null`), `allowed_hosts`, `env` (table), `user` (string or int), `environment_mode` (`"shared" | "separate" | null`), `[verifier.environment]` (same schema as `[environment]`).
- `[agent]`: `timeout_sec` (default null, meaning no timeout), `network_mode`, `allowed_hosts`, `user`.
- `[solution]`: `env` (table).
- `[environment]`: `build_timeout_sec` (default 600), `network_mode` (default "public"), `allowed_hosts`, `docker_image`, `os` ("linux" or "windows", default "linux"), `cpus`, `memory_mb`, `storage_mb`, `gpus`, `gpu_types`, `tpu` (`type`, `topology`), `allow_internet` (deprecated; prefer `network_mode`), `env`, `mcp_servers` (`name`, `transport`, `url`, `headers`, `command`, `args`), `skills_dir`, `healthcheck` (`command`, `interval_sec`, `timeout_sec`, `start_period_sec`, `start_interval_sec`, `retries`), `workdir`.

Example from the docs (values illustrative):
```toml
[verifier]
timeout_sec = 120.0
[agent]
timeout_sec = 120.0
[environment]
network_mode = "allowlist"
allowed_hosts = ["pypi.org"]
docker_image = "apple/unix-os:latest"
cpus = 1
memory_mb = 2048
storage_mb = 10240
```

**How files reach the container** (`/tasks/verifier`, `/tasks/solution`):
- `tests/` is uploaded to **`/tests/`** after the agent runs. `tests/test.sh` runs in the task working directory. The docs recommend absolute paths in the script.
- `solution/` is copied to **`/solution`**. Harbor runs `solve.sh` from the task working directory.
- Reward output: `/logs/verifier/reward.txt` or `/logs/verifier/reward.json`.

**Are tests hidden from the agent?** The docs do not say "hidden" in those words. They say `tests/` is uploaded after the agent runs, which implies the agent does not see them during its run. Treat that as an inference.

**Does the verifier run in the same container?** It depends on `verifier.environment_mode`:
- Default (both `environment_mode` and `[verifier.environment]` omitted): `"shared"`, which reuses the agent's container.

- Scaffolded tasks (`harbor task init`) set `verifier.environment_mode = "separate"`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

if pytest /tests/test_outputs.py; then
  echo 1 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
else
  echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
fi
```

### (2) `harbor run` CLI (`/jobs/run-a-job`, `/agents/pre-integrated-agents`)

Command shapes from the docs:
```bash
harbor run -p "<path/to/task>" -a "<agent>" -m "<model>"        # local task or dataset dir
harbor run -t "<org/task>@<ref>" -a "<agent>" -m "<model>"       # hub task
harbor run -d "<org/dataset>@<ref>" -a "<agent>" -m "<model>"    # hub dataset
harbor run --repo "<org/repo-name>" -p "<path/to/tasks>" -a "<agent>" -m "<model>"
harbor run -d "<dataset>@<version>" --registry-path "<path/to/registry.json>" -a "<agent>" -m "<model>"
harbor run -p "<path>" -a "<agent>" -m "<model>" -o "<jobs-dir>" --job-name "<job-name>"
harbor run -p "<path>" -a "<agent>" -m "<model>" -n "<concurrent>" -k "<attempts>" -r "<retries>"
harbor run -p "<path>" -a "<agent>" -m "<model>" -l "<max-tasks>" -i "<some-*-glob-pattern>" -x "<some-name>"
harbor run -p "<path>" -a "<agent>" -m "<model>" -e "<sandbox>" --allow-agent-host "<host>" --override-memory-mb "<memory-mb>"
harbor run -p "<path>" -a "<agent>" -m "<model>" --user-agent "<user-agent>" --user-model "<user-model>"
harbor run -a "<agent>" -m "<model>" --effort high
harbor run ... -a claude-code -m anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 --ak max_turns=20 --ae MCP_TIMEOUT=20000
harbor run ... -a codex --ak "config=path/to/config.toml"
harbor run ... -a opencode --ak skip_install=true

```

Flag meanings:
- `-p` path, `-t` task, `-d` dataset, `-a` agent, `-m`/`--model`.
- `-n` concurrency, `-k` attempts, `-r` retries.
- `-o` jobs dir, `--job-name`.
- `-l` max tasks, `-i` include glob, `-x` exclude name.
- `-e` sandbox, `--effort`, `--ak`/`--agent-kwarg` (repeatable), `--ae`/`--agent-env` (repeatable, values stay strings).
- `--print-config` prints the JobConfig. `--launch` runs on Harbor Hub (requires `harbor auth login`).
- `harbor run --help` lists everything.

The docs say `--ak` and `--ae` can be repeated, and `harbor run --help` is the authority for the full set.

**Model names:** Examples use `provider/model`, e.g. `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` and `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`. The docs say model names are parsed by LiteLLM, with the rules on `/agents/agent-auth-resolution`, which I did not read. I could not confirm the `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash` format for terminus-2.

**API keys:** The only documented example is `export OPENAI_API_KEY="..."` before `harbor run`. The docs also support `--ae` for agent env vars, and `${VAR}` references in `[verifier.env]` and `[environment.env]`, which read host env vars. The full per-provider list is in the agent-auth page, which I did not read.

### (3) Agents

- Names include `nop`, `oracle`, and `terminus-2`. The docs list about 40 names in total.
- **oracle:** Runs `solution/solve.sh`. It cannot run without a `solution/` folder. Supports Windows. Example for choosing among multiple solutions: `uv run harbor run -p examples/tasks/hello-world-multiple-solutions -a oracle --ae SOLUTION=2`. `SOLUTION` is the example's own variable, not a Harbor variable. `[solution.env]` overrides `--ae` for the same variable.
- **nop:** Supports Windows. No behavior was described in the pages I read. I could not confirm what it does, e.g. whether it leaves the reward at 0.
- **terminus-2:** Listed as ATIF-capable, MCP-capable, and skills-capable. No further behavior was described in the pages I read.
- Agent options: `--ak` is per-agent kwargs, `--ae` is agent env, and `skip_install=true` is for images that already contain the agent.

### (4) Output and trajectory format

- `-o` sets the jobs directory. `<job/path>/config.json` contains the resolved config.
- A trial's trajectory is `agent/trajectory.json` in the downloaded trial result. It is written to the agent log dir by agents with `capabilities.atif = true`.
- **ATIF is confirmed.** Current version is `ATIF-v1.8`. Top-level fields: `schema_version`, `session_id`, `agent` (`name`, `version`, `model_name`), `steps`, `trajectory_id`, `final_metrics`, `subagent_trajectories`, `extra`. Each step has `step_id` (sequential from 1), `source` (`user`/`agent`/system), `message`, and for agent steps optionally `tool_calls` (`tool_call_id`, `function_name`, `arguments`), `observation.results` (`source_call_id`, `content`), and `metrics`.
- Validate with `uv run python -m harbor.utils.trajectory_validator path/to/trajectory.json`.
- **result.json:** Not documented in any page I read. I could not confirm its location or fields.

### (5) Reward, timeouts, network

- **Reward files:** `/logs/verifier/reward.txt` (single number, "usually `1` or `0`") or `/logs/verifier/reward.json` (JSON object of labeled numeric metrics). If both exist, **Harbor prefers `reward.json`**.
- **Float/partial rewards:** The docs say "numerical reward" and reference labeled metrics in JSON. They do not explicitly say whether floats are accepted in `reward.txt`. The `multi_step_reward_strategy` field (`"mean"` or `"final"`) controls how multi-step rewards roll up.
- **Timeouts:** `verifier.timeout_sec` default 600. `agent.timeout_sec` default null (no timeout enforced). `environment.build_timeout_sec` default 600. The 120.0 values in the example are illustrative.
- **Internet:** `environment.network_mode` defaults to `"public"`. Options are `"no-network"`, `"public"`, `"allowlist"`, with `allowed_hosts` for allowlist. The deprecated `allow_internet` maps `false` to `no-network` and `true` to `public` when `network_mode` is omitted. `agent.network_mode` and `verifier.network_mode` override per phase. Some agents' built-in web tools are disabled under restricted policies.
- **Other gotchas:** Use absolute paths in `test.sh`. Use `.harborignore` and `.dockerignore` together. `skip_install` is needed when the sandbox has no internet and the agent is preinstalled.

```bash
if pytest /tests/test_outputs.py; then
  echo 1 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
else

fi
```
